clue.text: Staple I adapted, strengthening system

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered to suit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An office staple has been adapted into some kind of reinforcing mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is an exercise regime built around core strength, so it is a fitness method for strengthening the body.

clue.text: Second wing cut from baby fly

indicators.note: a word has two wings, its ends; cutting the second one removes its final letter

parts.note: a chick is a baby bird

explanation.surface: A young bird has one wing clipped and so cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a verb about the bird, but it is the adjective: in slang, fly means sharp and stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is informal slang for smart or stylish in appearance, which is what chic means.

clue.text: Old country covered in skyscrapers, I assumed

indicators.note: the answer is enclosed within the following words, wrapped up by them

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the I, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone supposes that some ancient land is now buried under tower blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the historic name of the country now called Iran, so it is a former nation.

clue.text: Catcher stands behind jumper, for example

parts.note: to back someone is to support or stand behind them
a jumper (a sweater) is an example of a top

explanation.surface: In a game, the catcher positions themselves behind a player who jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper in British English is a knitted sweater, a kind of top.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the catcher, who stops pitches behind the batter, is nicknamed the backstop.

clue.text: Clergy in battle, origin called into question

parts.note: Mons is a Belgian town, scene of a famous 1914 battle

indicators.note: something called into question is unsettled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Churchmen caught up in a conflict find the cause of it disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsignori is the plural of monsignor, an honorific title for senior Catholic priests, so a body of clergy.

clue.text: Tongue-in-cheek tweet after something brewing?

indicators.note: the word for tweet is to be placed following the brewing item

parts.note: tea is brewed in a pot
a bird's tweet is its song, so to tweet is to sing

explanation.surface: A jokey social-media post sent after making a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweet' suggests social media, but here it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing remarks are playful and not meant seriously, which is what tongue-in-cheek describes.

clue.text: Boat having dispensed with ballast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to ferry cargo to and from ships
second meaning: weighing less after dumping heavy material

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a vessel that has dropped its ballast; in fact the vessel and the reduced weight are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge for unloading ships is a lighter, and anything that has shed weight is lighter in the comparative sense.

clue.text: Title I think originally applied to pub

indicators.note: applied to means placed up against, so these pieces are attached after the pub

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a name that was first given to a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I think' reads as a hedge but splits: the numeral I and the initial of think.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronet is a hereditary British rank, so it is a title held by its bearer, styled Sir.

clue.text: Second-rate audio device with two items for computer user

parts.note: the first item: a key on the keyboard
the second item: the pointing device

explanation.surface: A cheap gadget sold with a couple of accessories for a PC owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse is an idiom for something amateurish or trivial, so it means inferior or second-rate.

clue.text: Put on fit striker?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means attached after, so the first word's piece comes second

parts.note: to fit or suit is to match
to stick something somewhere is to put it there

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction to put a fit striker on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer; it is the thing that is struck to light a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is struck against a box to ignite it, so it is literally a striker.

clue.text: Really, extremely unimpressive

parts.note: so as in 'is that so?', meaning really
so as in 'so good', meaning very or extremely

explanation.surface: Someone declares that something was truly and thoroughly underwhelming.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means merely middling or mediocre, which is something that fails to impress.

clue.text: Very dark when plane returned, fifty on board

indicators.note: something on board is inside a vessel, so this numeral goes within the other word

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: It was night when the aircraft came home with fifty passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' is not a turnaround signal here: it simply supplies the word for having come home.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet-black is the intense black of the gemstone jet, so it describes something extremely dark.

clue.text: Noted performance in high street premises?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a style of close-harmony singing, noted as in set to musical notes
second meaning: a shop where hair is cut

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' suggests famous, but it means musical, as in written in notes. A high street is a British town's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbershop is a genre of unaccompanied four-part harmony, and also the place where men's hair is trimmed.

clue.text: A drink in the empty African dish

indicators.note: in places the drink phrase inside the emptied word
an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A drink is served in an African bowl that has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew, named after its conical earthenware pot, so a dish from Africa.

clue.text: Eatery ultimately gross, open a different diner!

indicators.note: different letters arrangement: the following words are made into something else
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is used

explanation.surface: A restaurant is disgusting, so someone suggests opening another diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eatery' looks like the definition but only gives its last letter; the definition is the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is a cheap, basic café serving fried food, an informal name for a diner.

clue.text: Direction taken in change of rate, forward

indicators.note: taken in means admitted inside, so one piece sits within the other
a change of something alters it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tack is a sailing course or direction

explanation.surface: A shift in pace dictates the route taken going ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and other team sports, a forward is an attacking player, an attacker.

clue.text: Sticky food, honey

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thick sugar syrup
second meaning: a British term of endearment, like darling

explanation.walkthrough: 'honey' looks like another sticky food, but it is the endearment; treacle is used affectionately in London speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is syrup from sugar refining, and in British slang it is an affectionate form of address like sweetheart.

clue.text: Conflict's ending with intensity on battlefield

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: heat as in the heat of the moment, intensity

explanation.surface: A war's climax plays out fiercely on the field of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the region where fighting takes place, so it means a battlefield.

clue.text: Passionate gardener finally filling a hole

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so this letter goes within the other words
finally means at the end, so just the last letter is kept

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: A keen gardener fills in a hole in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning with feeling, eager and fervent, so it is a synonym for passionate.

clue.text: Clear off, Tories!

parts.note: off as in out, not on
the Tories are the British party of the political right

explanation.surface: A protester shouts at Conservatives to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear off' reads as one phrase, but it splits: Clear is the definition. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright win is a clear, unqualified one, so outright means clear or complete.

clue.text: Fluid has met water flowing through capital

indicators.note: something fluid is not fixed in shape, so these letters can flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Some liquid has encountered water running through a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river that runs through London, the British capital.

clue.text: Almost entirely disorientated touring a country in Asia

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the shortened word wraps around a letter
almost all of the word is used, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: A traveller gets thoroughly lost while on a trip around an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked nation in Southeast Asia, bordering Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: Republican supporter playing a part, you may count on me!

parts.note: a supporting actor sharing the billing

explanation.surface: A political party backer, active in a campaign, assures everyone they are reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' suggests US politics, but it means a citizen of a republic, here one in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a republic, so a Costa Rican is a citizen of that republic, a Republican of a sort.

clue.text: Short distance, walk in the park, heading off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy, as is a walk in the park

explanation.surface: A brief stroll in the park as someone sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, so it serves as a byword for a tiny distance.

clue.text: Setter welcomed into family was prosperous

indicators.note: something welcomed into a group is taken inside it

parts.note: blood as in kin, one's family
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler was adopted into a household that was wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to flourish, so bloomed means thrived or did well, matching was prosperous.

clue.text: Out-of-this-world heavy metal singer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the planet nearest the Sun
second meaning: the dense liquid element quicksilver
third meaning: Freddie, lead vocalist of Queen

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a rock vocalist; it is three separate meanings: a planet, a chemical element and a famous singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a planet beyond Earth, a dense metallic element, and the surname of Queen's Freddie Mercury.
